intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple portal component that dynamically renders content from one part of your Angular application into another. You will learn the core concept of content projection using Angular's built-in portal and portal outlet features. The main technologies involved are Angular's ComponentFactoryResolver, ViewContainerRef, and the CdkPortal and CdkPortalOutlet directives from the Angular CDK. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible, reusable UI components that can inject content anywhere in your app's DOM structure.
intro.usecase: Portals in Angular enable developers to render UI components outside their normal DOM hierarchy while maintaining Angular's data binding and lifecycle management. This pattern is essential for creating modal dialogs, tooltips, and notifications that need to appear above other content without CSS positioning hacks. In real applications, portals power dashboard widgets that can be dragged between panels, complex form wizards with floating validation messages, and contextual help panels that overlay specific interface sections. Developers use portals to build maintainable, reusable overlay components that work predictably across different parts of their application.
